What is the relationship between Dzongkha and Tibetan? It has a much more distant relationship to Standard Tibetan. Spoken Dzongkha and Tibetan are around 50% to 80% mutually intelligible, with the literary forms of both highly influenced by the liturgical (clerical) Classical Tibetan language, known in Bhutan as Chöke (ཆོས་སྐད །), which has been used for centuries by Buddhist monks. Is Dzongkha a language? Dzongkha was declared the national language of Bhutan in 1971. Dzongkha study is mandatory in all schools, and the language is the lingua franca in the districts to the south and east where it is not the mother tongue. The Bhutanese films Travellers and Magicians (2003) and Lunana: A Yak in the Classroom (2019) are in Dzongkha. What are Dzongkha verbs? Dzongkha verbs are mainly marked for the progressive (དོ་ -do), the witnessed past (ཡི་ -yi; ཅི་ -ci), the inferred past (ནུག་ -nu), the perfective (སོ་ so), the present continuous (པའི་སྒང་ ‑bigang ~ ‑migang; བའི་སྒང་ ‑wigang), the adhortative (གེ་ ‑ge), the optative (བཅུག་ cu), and the supine (པར་ ‑ba ~ -ma; བར་ ‑wa).
